name: Manioc and squash cultivation in the Llanos de Moxos
summary: Phytoliths from dated forest islands in Bolivia's Llanos de Moxos show people cultivating manioc and squash there more than 10,000 years ago, in a proposed early centre of plant domestication.
description: Phytolith analysis of radiocarbon-dated deposits in the Llanos de Moxos, Bolivia, documents cultivation of manioc at about 10,350 and squash at about 10,250 calibrated years before present. The same people began creating artificial forest islands in the seasonally flooded savannah from about 10,850 years before present, eventually about 4,700 of them. The paper documents cultivation; it does not show that the plants were already domesticated.

impact.note: The paper names this region as a proposed centre of manioc domestication, and manioc became a staple across lowland South America and later the tropics (reach 2); cultivation gave foragers a new capability but the evidence is not yet a farming way of life (depth 2); manioc processing methods are its few known successors (generativity 1).

unresolved.note: Whether the phytoliths show domesticated plants or cultivated wild ones, and the genetic evidence for where manioc was domesticated (not reached).
Independence from Andean and north-western South American centres.
Which forest-island sites gave the manioc and squash phytoliths; only the abstract was read, the full text being behind a subscription.

research.note: The paper says south-western Amazonia had been proposed as an early centre of plant domestication on genetic grounds and confirms early cultivation there, but the part read does not say these crops were reached without knowledge of other American centres.
